data.narrative:
Mujin, a Series C robotics and manufacturing company founded by Issei Takino and Rosen Diankov, has raised $85M+ to date. The valuation analysis draws from a comp universe of 9 private peers (including Hadrian, Agile Robots, and Nimble Robotics) and 1 public comparable.

Two triangulation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis uses the $85M total raised as a proxy base value and applies a 1.7x multiplier typical for Series C advancement, implying a valuation of $144M. Peer-median analysis across three same-sector, same-stage comparables yields a median valuation of $1.0B, with a range spanning $1.0B to $1.6B. The peer set reflects material heterogeneity in late-stage robotics valuations.

The triangulated analysis implies a valuation range of $123M (low) to $1.1B (high), with a median of $572M. The substantial spread reflects genuine methodological divergence: stage-progression mechanically anchors to capital deployed, while peer-median reflects market consensus valuations for later-stage robotics companies. Key uncertainties include capital efficiency relative to peer cohort, customer concentration, and execution risk on manufacturing automation adoption rates. Resolution of these factors would narrow the range materially.
